name: Ultracol

card.summary: A Korean polydioxanone (PDO) microsphere collagen-stimulating injectable (Ultra V UltraCol 200) used in clinics to improve skin quality, facial volume and nasolabial folds.
card.aka: Ultra V collagen; Ultra V UltraCol 200; PDO microspheres
card.note: Clinic-administered injectable; one published trial of the product has been retracted.

quick.overview:
Ultracol (Ultra V UltraCol 200) is an injectable made of polydioxanone (PDO) microspheres, sold as a collagen biostimulator. Clinics use it to improve skin texture, add gentle volume and soften lines such as the nasolabial folds. The idea is that the microspheres prompt the body to build new collagen over time.

A small pilot study in 20 patients aged 40 to 80 reported better facial volume, contour and nasolabial fold depth at 2 months. An earlier 31-participant study on nasolabial folds was later retracted, so the published base is small.
quick.how: It is injected by a clinician, in the pilot study using a cannula technique in a single session, sometimes combined with other agents. Results are assessed over weeks to months as collagen builds.
quick.risks: As an injectable filler-type product it carries general risks of injection procedures, such as swelling, bruising, lumps and infection, and rarer vascular complications. It should be administered by a qualified clinician, and regulatory approval varies by country.

lead: Ultracol, marketed as Ultra V UltraCol 200, is a Korean injectable whose main component is polydioxanone (PDO) in microsphere form. It is described as a collagen biostimulator: rather than only filling space, it is meant to stimulate the skin to produce collagen [1].

Clinics use it to improve skin quality and facial contour. A 2026 pilot study in Cureus treated 20 patients aged 40 to 80 with Ultracol plus organic silicon using a facial 'adipostructuring' technique and reported more facial volume and contour definition, shallower nasolabial folds and improved positioning of the cheek region at 10 days and 2 months, assessed by a blinded evaluator [1].
An earlier study of 31 participants evaluating Ultracol 200 on nasolabial folds was published in Skin Research and Technology in 2024 and later retracted in 2025 [2][3].

chain: PDO microspheres injected into the skin or subcutaneous layer
Smoother skin, softer folds, more cheek volume
angle.text: Clinics inject it so that treated areas gain collagen and subtle volume over time. People choose it to refresh skin texture and soften nasolabial folds without surgery.

paras: Ultracol is referred to in the literature as a polydioxanone collagen biostimulator, commonly described as PDO microspheres [1]. PDO is a material also used in absorbable sutures and threads.

In the 2026 pilot report, clinicians added organic silicon to the product and placed it with a 22-gauge cannula, 2.5 mL per side of the face in one session, aiming at the mid-face and cheeks [1]. Outcomes were judged from photographs by a blinded evaluator and a patient satisfaction survey [1].

A 2026 pilot study of 20 patients aged 40 to 80 reported improved facial three-dimensionality, volumetric projection and contour, reduced nasolabial fold depth and improved vertical positioning of the malar region at 10 days and 2 months [1].

A 2024 study of 31 participants aged 20 to 59 compared Ultracol 200 with other products and reported improved skin texture and wrinkle volume measured by 3D imaging, with satisfactory responses from participants [3]. That paper was retracted in 2025 [2].

The retraction of one study means the published base is smaller than it first appeared [2]. General risks of dermal injectables include bruising, swelling, nodules and infection. Treatment by an unqualified provider raises risks.

timeline.event: A study of Ultracol 200 on nasolabial folds is published in Skin Research and Technology [3].
A pilot study in Cureus reports results of Ultracol with organic silicon in 20 older patients [1].
